A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDVI/DDTD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original convergence, runtime, scaling, control, and model-error experiments in Section 6 and Appendices 11–13.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds discount-factor comparisons in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: The DDVI updates, deflation constructions, AutoPI/AutoQR procedures, and DDTD model-update mechanism are retained. The new simplified AutoPI pseudocode specializes the existing algorithm; state-dependent stepsize notation clarifies behavior already covered by v1.

E1.justification: The same four environment families and policy-evaluation/control tasks remain. However, Chain Walk is re-specified: positive/negative rewards move from states 3/50 to 40/11, and movement probabilities change, including successful movement from 80% to 70%. This revises an existing environment scenario without broadening the research domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain VI, Anderson VI, S-AVI, PID VI, and Anchored VI for DDVI, and TD Learning and Dyna for DDTD. Added discount-factor experiments use the existing comparator sets; new Dyna citations do not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: The rank comparison changes its discount factor from 0.995 to 0.99, reduces QR iterations from 600 to 100, and charges QR initialization as equivalent VI iterations. Evaluation-policy specifications and Figure 2's reported Garnet branching factor also change, the latter from 3 to 2. New DDTD experiments use discount 0.95 and 5,000 samples. These substantially revise settings and computational-cost accounting; retained plots do not establish that all affected experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F extends rank sensitivity across discount factors 0.95, 0.99, and 0.995. Appendix G adds discount-0.95 DDTD comparisons across the existing three model-error levels. These extend existing sensitivity and robustness questions; the earlier horizon-scaling and model-error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20-instance Garnet averages, 100-instance Garnet control averages, and 20-run DDTD averages with standard-error shading. The added DDTD panels follow the same reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 1 is replaced under revised settings, and Figures 8–9 and the lower panels of Figures 14–15 add convergence results. The new discount-0.95 rank plots show that QR initialization can make higher fixed ranks slower overall than VI. Most matched earlier plots retain their results. These are bounded additions and replacements, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the general SOR derivation from alpha C minus (alpha minus 1)D to alpha C plus (alpha minus 1)D. The principal convergence theorems remain, including the non-asymptotic DDTD bounds already present in v1 Appendix 8.6 and retained in v2 Appendix B.6.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: acceleration through deflation and matrix splitting, eigenvalue-dependent convergence guarantees, the DDTD extension, and empirical effectiveness. Added experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds an explicit interpretation of DDTD as hybrid model-free/model-based learning and an associated computational-efficiency claim. The conclusion adds function approximation for large or continuous spaces as future work. Existing qualifications concerning control and model error are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an experimental source-code link, QR computational-cost details, and a hyperparameter table for discount-0.95 Maze experiments. Appendix D rewrites policy documentation, explicitly distinguishing Maze policies used for DDVI and DDTD. The link's external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bedaywi et al. (2024) on PID-accelerated TD and Sutton (1990) on Dyna. Appendix A adds convergence-rate comparisons for S-AVI, PID VI, and Anchored VI. The broader positioning and multiple-eigenvalue-deflation novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the SOR and AutoPI explanations, edits language, promotes the QR algorithm into Section 4.3, and reorganizes appendix labels. Author information and acknowledgments change. These are localized revisions within a largely retained narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different journal layout, including typography, margins, running headers, and author block. Figure 1 is redrawn with changed axes and computational-cost offsets; environment diagrams are revised; two rank-comparison figures are added; DDTD figures gain additional panel rows; and tables are reformatted with one added hyperparameter table.

improvement.justification: Accounting for QR initialization makes the rank comparisons more informative, while additional discount-factor tests, the SOR sign correction, clearer explanations, and a code pointer provide useful gains. These remain limited improvements to an already developed study. Revised setting descriptions accompanying retained plots leave some experimental provenance unresolved, tempering the reproducibility benefit.
